bullets: Leading-edge multi-die assemblies require a shift from rigid pass/fail testing to context-aware outlier detection to prevent field failures.

backlog.title: This founder is making cheaper, cleaner steel
backlog.summary: The steel industry isn’t exactly known for innovation. Very little has changed about purifying iron ore since the process was invented and commercialized in the 1850s. The majority of steelmakers melt solid iron ore at dizzyingly high temperatures inside blast furnaces, where the material reacts with gases to trigger chemical reactions that remove oxygen. It…
bullets: Hertha Metals has developed a single-step furnace process that replaces coal with natural gas to refine iron ore into liquid steel.
The technology claims to reduce carbon emissions by at least 50% while simultaneously cutting production costs by 25% compared to traditional blast furnace methods.
Given that steel production accounts for roughly 7% of global carbon emissions, this innovation offers a scalable path to decarbonization that aligns with the industry's tight profit margins.

Design teams are now prioritizing 'token efficiency' to ensure that the ROI of AI tools justifies the operational expense of running large language models.
Industry experts warn that while AI offers design acceleration, the high cost of potential errors in chip manufacturing makes verification and trust in AI outputs more critical than ever.

backlog.title: When Digital Forensics Reaches The Hardware Layer
backlog.summary:
Security controls are increasingly implemented in ways that can limit access to information required for an investigation.
The post When Digital Forensics Reaches The Hardware Layer appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Modern hardware-based security features like Secure Boot, TEEs, and encrypted storage are increasingly blocking traditional software-level forensic data extraction.
Forensic investigators are now forced to pivot toward hardware security testing to bypass physical protections that restrict access to stored data.
Successful investigations now require deep expertise in hardware architecture, schematics, and silicon-level security implementations rather than just software analysis.

backlog.title: System-Level Test In The AI Era: Validating Reliability At Scale
backlog.summary:
Passing ATE no longer guarantees success in the field as sustained, high-power workloads push thermal and electrical limits. 
The post System-Level Test In The AI Era: Validating Reliability At Scale appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Automated Test Equipment (ATE) is no longer sufficient for AI-era chips, as it fails to capture failure modes that only emerge during sustained, high-power system operation.
System-Level Test (SLT) is becoming a mandatory complement to ATE, providing the necessary environmental and workload context to validate reliability at scale.
Advanced packaging architectures like 2.5D and 3D integration have increased thermal and interconnect complexity, making system-level validation a first-order requirement for modern HPC modules.

backlog.title: Validation Gets Tested At 1kW
backlog.summary:
Kilowatt-class AI accelerators are forcing engineers to rethink what counts as adequate coverage across workload, thermal behavior, test hardware, and time.
The post Validation Gets Tested At 1kW appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Kilowatt-class AI accelerators require validation of the entire physical ecosystem, including cooling and test hardware, rather than just the silicon itself.
Standard electrical fault coverage is no longer sufficient; engineers must now correlate fault coverage with thermal coverage to ensure reliability under sustained high-power workloads.
Transient analysis is becoming critical, as different AI workloads can trigger localized thermal stress that leads to failures even if the device passes static power tests.

For clinicians, operators, and administrative teams who…

The revenue cycle is emerging as a critical proving ground for AI, as it involves high-volume transactions and complex reasoning across disparate systems like billing, insurance, and clinical documentation.

Healthcare leaders are cautioned against confusing model capability with operational capability, noting that successful integration requires reasoning across the entire chain of administrative decisions.

backlog.title: Capital and Nomos: The Political Economy of the Interregnum
backlog.summary:
The post-Cold War liberal order has come to an end. Every serious analyst across the political spectrum acknowledges this, even if the acknowledgment arrives wrapped in euphemism: “strategic autonomy,” “de-risking,” or “friend-shoring,” i.e., the polite vocabulary of elites who destroyed a world order and cannot quite bring themselves to say so plainly. The neoliberal settlement,…
Continue reading Capital and Nomos: The Political Economy of the Interregnum on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: The post-Cold War neoliberal order has collapsed as both an intellectual framework and a functional reality, marked by the failure of financialization and the hollowing out of Western manufacturing bases.

Key structural milestones in this decline include the 2008 financial crisis, China's industrial ascent, and the 2014 annexation of Crimea, which collectively exposed the fragility of the liberal international system.

A shift is occurring within policy-minded circles toward prioritizing national interest, de-risking from China, and re-industrialization, signaling a move away from purely financialized economic governance.

The current 'interregnum' is characterized by an institutional shell attempting to maintain influence while the underlying political and economic consensus has already shifted toward state-led productive economies.

backlog.title: How Ukrainian Drones Are Exploiting Soviet-Era Geography
backlog.summary:
As Cold War-era geography meets modern warfare, the ironies are striking. For centuries, distance was one of Russia's greatest military assets. Napoleon, Hitler, and NATO all confronted the problem of Russia’s immense landscape. But the overconcentrated and isolated infrastructure established by the Soviets now forces Russia to defend some of the farthest corners of its territory. 
Continue reading How Ukrainian Drones Are Exploiting Soviet-Era Geography on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: Ukraine has successfully targeted all eleven of Russia's largest oil refineries, demonstrating the capability to strike critical infrastructure up to 2,500 kilometers from the border.
The conflict has evolved into a laboratory for AI-assisted drone warfare, with autonomous terminal guidance systems allowing for precise, long-range strikes against logistics hubs like Wildberries.

Soviet-era industrial design, characterized by centralized production and reliance on strategic depth, has become a significant liability as modern drone swarms bypass traditional geographic defenses.

The war highlights a fundamental shift in economic geography where concentrated industrial assets are increasingly vulnerable, forcing a reevaluation of infrastructure security in the age of low-cost, long-range autonomous weapons.

backlog.title: The Automation Paradox: America’s Hidden Bottleneck to Reindustrialization
backlog.summary:
As an engineer, I ran maintenance for a Fortune 500 pulp and paper company. I was based at a plant in Tennessee and covered nine other facilities across the Southeast and Florida. For anyone unfamiliar with heavy industry, these plants are filled with massive, capital-intensive equipment: three-story machines stretching the length of a football field,…
Continue reading The Automation Paradox: America’s Hidden Bottleneck to Reindustrialization on American Affairs Journal.
bullets: Industrial re-shoring faces a critical bottleneck in the loss of 'tribal knowledge' held by veteran technicians, which is essential for maintaining aging, modified brownfield infrastructure.
Modern digital documentation and cloud-based dashboards often fail to capture the nuanced, three-dimensional expertise required to diagnose and repair legacy machinery during high-stakes downtime.
The reliance on undocumented, veteran-specific expertise creates a significant operational risk for capital-intensive industries where unplanned downtime can cost millions per hour.

The gap between theoretical manuals and the reality of century-old, heavily modified equipment suggests that automation and re-industrialization efforts may be hindered by a lack of skilled human capital.

backlog.title: Can the US battery market untangle from China?
backlog.summary: The US is hitting records for the rapid growth of its energy storage market. That’ll go a long way to shoring up the grid, increasing reliability and also cutting emissions, since batteries can help store energy from intermittent renewables like wind and solar. Crucially, this is all happening with the help of cheap Chinese batteries,…
bullets: The US government has escalated its decoupling strategy by issuing an executive order that effectively bans Chinese-produced batteries and power equipment from grid-scale energy storage systems.
New legislation mandates that starting in 2026, 55% of material costs for energy storage projects must originate outside of China and other restricted countries to qualify for federal tax credits.

These protectionist policies, combined with import tariffs raised to 25%, force a trade-off between the rapid, low-cost deployment of renewable energy and the long-term goal of domestic supply chain independence.

Verification Capture Points are being introduced as structured artifacts to ensure traceability across complex, multi-die system designs.

backlog.title: Accelerating Shift Left With Early RTL DFT Analysis And Connectivity Verification
backlog.summary:
How early RTL testability analysis and DFT optimization enable shift left strategies that improve manufacturing test quality, reduce turnaround time, and deliver early quality estimates.

bullets: Early RTL-level testability analysis is critical for identifying DFT violations before synthesis, preventing costly late-stage design re-spins.
New methodologies allow for early ATPG coverage estimation with up to 95-99% correlation to final silicon results, enabling faster time-to-market.
Automated structural checks and hard-to-detect fault analysis are being used to optimize test point selection, directly reducing manufacturing test costs.

backlog.title: Beyond Conventional Ring Oscillators: Purpose-Built Process Detectors For Deeper Silicon Insight
backlog.summary:
How design-aware monitor analytics connects production measurements with device behavior and pre-silicon expectations.
The post Beyond Conventional Ring Oscillators: Purpose-Built Process Detectors For Deeper Silicon Insight appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Conventional ring oscillators are increasingly limited because they compress multiple device and interconnect effects into a single frequency value, masking specific process shifts.
Purpose-built Global Variation Process Detectors (GPD) allow for better isolation of NMOS, PMOS, and interconnect variations through controlled structural diversity.
The industry is moving toward design-aware analytics that translate raw monitor measurements into actionable intelligence regarding device-level behavior.

backlog.title: Beyond Thickness: Using Picosecond Ultrasonic Technology For SiCr Process Control In BCD Devices
backlog.summary:
Improve visibility into deposition variation by combining thickness metrology with simultaneous reflectivity measurements.
The post Beyond Thickness: Using Picosecond Ultrasonic Technology For SiCr Process Control In BCD Devices appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Picosecond ultrasonic technology is being deployed to measure thin-film thickness in BCD devices using non-destructive, laser-generated acoustic waves.

Thickness measurements alone are insufficient for SiCr process control, as variations in microstructure and density can significantly impact electrical characteristics like TCR and long-term stability.
By combining thickness data with simultaneous reflectivity measurements, manufacturers can detect process excursions earlier in the production cycle to improve yield.

backlog.title: This road map could help us decide whether to deploy solar geoengineering
backlog.summary: A San Francisco nonprofit has published a detailed road map of the experiments, studies, and infrastructure that it says would be needed to make informed decisions about the use of solar geoengineering, MIT Technology Review can reveal. Scientists have now spent half a century exploring the possibility that we could counteract climate change by releasing…
bullets: The nonprofit Reflective has released a comprehensive SAI Research Roadmap to standardize the study of stratospheric aerosol injection as a climate intervention tool.

The report estimates that a coordinated global research effort would require a decade and $370 million, whereas an uncoordinated approach could double the time and nearly quadruple the cost to $1.4 billion.

The proposal remains highly controversial, with many academics advocating for a total ban on outdoor experiments due to concerns over global equity and the inability to govern such powerful technology.

backlog.title: Understanding the thermal ceiling in portable power
backlog.summary: Plug a phone into a modern charger and the first 10 minutes are impressive. The next 20 are not. This is not a defect. It’s the connected device protecting itself. As temperature rises during charging, a smartphone’s battery management system reduces the current it will accept, because heat accelerates the chemical degradation that permanently reduces…
bullets: Portable power performance is constrained by thermal limits rather than raw wattage, as devices throttle charging speeds to prevent chemical degradation of batteries.
A significant 'specification gap' exists where products are marketed by peak wattage, which is rarely sustainable in real-world conditions due to heat accumulation.
Magnetic wireless charging exacerbates thermal issues by placing heat sources in direct contact with the device, limiting the effectiveness of passive dissipation materials like graphite sheets.
